This is one of those games where I wish I could give it a neutral recommendation.  I'm giving it a positive review, but just barely.

See, the game starts out fairly strong, with a charming plot and characters.  I love the idea of a retired supervillain having to come out of retirement to go on a quest that will lead to him becoming a hero against his will and save the world.  And the idea of a supervillain retirement community, where the game begins, is just great. 

The problem is that this all falls apart about halfway through the game.  Boyle, the supervillain main character, gets shoved into the background and turned into a joke as more characters are introduced, with a new, far less interesting elf character taking his place as the protagonist.  The plot also gets bogged down into really annoying fetch quests and then gets wrapped up in a sequel hook for a sequel that never happened.  

As for the gameplay, it starts out rough and then becomes tedious.  Maps are maze like and take forever to traverse due to the characters' slow movement speed, which is combined with TONS of backtracking in those fetch quests.   This all comes to a head in an absolutely infuriating puzzle section in the middle half where, if you don't have a guide, you'll probably end up pulling your hair out.   Combat is fine, but lackluster.  There's no depth to it and you have to do a fair amount of grinding in the latter half of the game. 

In the hands of a better writer and designer, this could have been something really special.  Instead it's just okay.   Get it on sale and give it a shot, just be prepared for when the wheels come off.

For those unfamiliar with the series, this is an RPG that focuses heavily on fetch quests, with a fairly simple combat system.  If you love being a master battle tactician, this is not the game for you.  There is a really impressive depth of quests here, and most of the characters have their own individual journeys to explore.  There is a much greater sense of getting to know the characters.  Robin's shop was a particularly good add-on.

A few points to decide whether this game is for you:
- It focuses on fetch quests, not fighting. However, I was impressed with the way that the very simple combat system was expanded with new options, for example being able to equip Hi'beru with books that gave him different spells. Another very clever touch was that Robin's abilities depend on who else is in the active party.
- There is a lot of walking backwards and forwards, so some patience is required.  The amount of pointless walking has been cut back massively from Aveyond 3 (thank goodness) but travelling is still lumpy in places.  The maze-like quality of maps has also reduced to an extent, but some of the early areas may be frustrating if you don't make a quick sketch.
- It uses a humorous storyline rather than going for the serious take of its predecessor.  Personally I enjoyed this; it gave it a fresh angle and plenty of originality.  The ending was weak and very abrupt, but much of the story's purpose comes from following the journeys of the characters anyway, so saving the world is an afterthought.
- A very detailed free guide is available online, so there's no getting stuck working out what to do.

Overall, a solid recommend.

Overall, Aveyond 4 ended up being a nice, unexpected find for me. If you tend to enjoy humorous, top-down, turn-based RPGs, I'd recommend looking into it.

Boyle and the rest of the cast you gather are enjoyable and all play a little differently--only one character has a traditional MP gauge, and another can swap out their combat skills be equipping different tomes, for example. Each of them bring some value to the story, but they are also given additional side quests that focus more specifically on them, which is something I appreciated. The earliest characters you get naturally have the most time to shine, but even the later ones have interesting subplots and personal quests to build on them. All of them get nice art portraits for a full range of emotions, which benefits the storytelling and comedy delivery.

The world and dungeons are relatively scenic and nice to look at, but several of them felt bigger than they need to be. This emptiness was compounded by the fact that many groups of enemies don't respawn, so there's a lot of open terrain once you clear foes out (admittedly, both a good and bad thing in my book). There are some missions and sidequests that involve backtracking to old areas, but the game does offer additional modes of transportation. It alleviates some of the tedium of returning to areas after you've thoroughly cleaned them out, but not entirely (one mode still involves a decent bit of walking around to get where you need to go).

The music and sound effects are generally solid, though many of the areas are filled with ambient noise tracks instead of music. I personally liked this choice as a change of pace (though I did start noticing the same sounds again and again in some areas, like wolf howls at night). I also ran into some sound glitches where music cut out (often after combat), and the only way to bring it back was to exit the area and return.

I played the game on its hard setting, and I ultimately finished it in about 38 hours. You should consider this mark to be on the -very- high end of playtime, as I tend to take my sweet time going through RPGs and try to do everything I possibly can. Some of that time was due to a number of quests being convoluted; I had to wander for a while until I could find some of the tools that Ingrid the Witch uses to make her potions, for example. There's also a little bit of additional replay value, as you're offered some choices in the game that affect the character's interactions and the battle skills they get.

I realize it's hard to recommend games nowadays when it feels like everyone has a backlog going through the roof. There's a lot of options out there. But I feel that Aveyond 4 showcases a lot of passion from its developers and offers a versatile experience (that also has some fun poking at the common tropes without getting -too- cheeky about it). I definitely enjoyed my time with the game, and I'd give it a thought if you're looking for another RPG to add to your collection.

I love the Aveyond series!  This was a welcome addition to the Aveyond series and was a welcome return to their previous all in one game format (as opposed to breaking out the game into several parts/chapters like they did with Aveyond 3).  However the game is far from the best Aveyond game and it has some drawbacks.

This is a pixel graphic RPG and if you've liked other Aveyond games or other similar RPGs you will likely enjoy this one too.  It has a pretty good story and lots of humor (much of it's a little corny but in a good way... usually).  I love that the militant squirrels made a more prominent return.  The story starts off strong but it begins to lag in the middle.  The end is a little bit of a let down.  It gets pulled in a lot of different directions which gets a little difficult to follow making it sometimes difficult to figure out where you need to go to progress to the next part in the story.  There is a vast number of side quests available but one of the drawbacks is that main quests and side quests all involve an excessive amount of back and forth.  I don't like these kind of games to be completely linear but keeping a large number of quests relatively close to each other in the same region is generally preferable.  It feels like you are walking back and forth for almost everything and you have to do a lot of backtracking.  This is made worse by the slow walking pace (which can't be adjusted and unlike other games there are no speed boots that let you walk faster) and lack of quick teleport system.  There is an odd array of mist portals and later ship ports but it doesn't feel much shorter to use them... you will walk back and forth a lot.  Not quite as bad as Aveyond 3 but definitely more-so than other Aveyond games.

The graphics are good for pixel RPG style.  There are great backgrounds with lots of detail and variations for different areas.  The sprites are good and there's plenty of variation with little repeat.  The animations are about what you'd expect for the style.  Most of the Character portraits are good but there are some odd looking parts and it feels like some character portraits were given a lot of time and artistry while others feel lower quality, maybe rushed?  But they are still good.  The small animations when the characters are happy vs. unhappy are cute.

The sound is pretty good.  There's decent background music that's different for the various areas.  Some of the battle sounds are really weird but most of them are fine.  The squirrels in the castle are super weird sounding.

The menu interface is a bit different compared to other aveyond games.  If this is your first Aveyond game you will probably not have an issue but if you played other Aveyond games you might find it confusing at first and it may require a bit of getting used to.

Personally, I like to explore all areas and complete every quest so I found it very frustrating that there appeared to be areas I never could get to.  There are two islands that are covered in a bubble and little lands to their sides.  I could never find a way to access them even though I'm sure it's insanely easy or something.  I could pull my ship up to the little islands but nut not enter the dungeon cells.  I'm certain there's more that I could have done but it's difficult to figure out how or where I needed to go to do it and because there's already so much back and forth in non-straightforward ways it gets confusing where you've searched already or not.  I saved before the final battle so I might have to go back and try again to access those other areas.

I liked the addition of an item that helps you find all the goodie caves.  It saved me a lot of time and clicks testing out every wall for those hidden entrances.  I didn't like that you don't really have a character house at any point where you can all go and rest for free.  You must rely on inns the entire time throughout the game which is a bit different than other Aveyond games.  I also found the store that you get later in the game was somewhat entertaining but also pretty useless... why couldn't we have just sold the items to vendors like all the other Aveyond games instead of having unsaleable junk that you can only get rid of once you get a store.

Though there appears to be more I could have done, I reached made it to the end (exploring everything I could finishing every side quest I could, and buying everything I could find) in about 14 hours.  If you are buying it at full price that works out to about $1/hr of gameplay which is pretty good.  If you can get it on sale though t's an even better deal.

Il protagonista Boyle è un soggettone che vuole fare il cattivone (in passato lo era) ed è promesso sposo ad una strega cattiva (Ingrid): i due si beccano in continuazione durante tutto il gioco, e non solo, ci sono stati momenti con altri personaggi davvero piacevoli, che mi hanno appunto strappato più risate.
Il gioco è lungo (tra 35 e 40 ore se si decide di portare tutte le missioni a termine), anche se per qualche missione permane il problema del backtracking (soprattutto una quest relativa alla formazione di una congrega delle streghe, ma ne vale la pena per avere una maledizione finale che fa un fracco di danni).

Le missioni sono appuntate su un diario e mano a mano che si risolvono vengono cancellate, quindi il tutto è molto pulito e ordinato. Anche se l'uso dell'inventario per gestire gli oggetti è molto scomodo, perchè bisogna scorrerli sempre uno ad uno non potendo gestire le loro priorità (ad esempio, se durante un combattimento un personaggio muore bisogna scorrere tutti gli oggetti per trovare quello che permette la resurrezione e questo viene messo in fondo alla lista).

C'è molto di avventura grafica oltre ai combattimenti, con enigmi (bella la parte dentro il castello in cui bisogna capire cosa fare per procedere tra le stanze inizialmente inibite) e la disposizione dei mondi verso cui viaggiare è abbastanza intelligente, anche se a volte si dimenticano i nomi delle locazioni e si fa fatica a ricordare dove andare. Ma c'è anche una specie di netherworld che permette di fare viaggi veloci e leggere i nomi delle locazioni di arrivo su comodi cartelli. Verso la fine si sblocca anche la nave e si può anche viaggiare liberamente.

A parte il backtraking (che per questa tipologia di gioco è sempre presente e a volte è snervante perchè alcuni passaggi sono labirintici e si vorrebbe evitare di rifarli più volte) evidenzio tre altri difetti:

1- le missioni secondarie sono piacevoli, ma a volte lo sforzo non dà grandi soddisfazioni finali, o perchè l'oggetto acquisito è inutile o perchè magari in precedenza si era già presa un'arma (o armatura) potente in un'altra missione e ci si ritrova come premio di missione qualcosa di più scarso. Inoltre le missioni non rilasciano esperienza: secondo me avrebbero dovuto implementarla. Anche perchè...

2- la sezione finale è davvero sproporzionata in quanto a difficoltà rispetto il resto del gioco (non impareranno mai a gestire questo aspetto, mai). In genere combattimenti contro nemici nuovi e boss sono piacevoli e ben misurati, ma poi si arriva sulla Montagna del Teschio e si scopre di avere di fronte nemici troppo OverPowered, boss finale compreso. Qui ho faticato un po', e sono stato costretto a tornare indietro per finire altre missioni, trovando armature migliori, e livellare maggiormente.

3- la trama generale non è proprio chiara e nel complesso non ha molto mordente. Per fortuna Boyle ed Ingrid tengono alto lo spirito dell'avventura.

Belle le locazioni, belle alcune pensate (interruttori che modificano ad esempio la conformazione di un livello) e bella la sequenza finale (con battuta epica finale di Boyle) in cui si inserisce anche una sequenza che dipende dalla romance intrapresa durante il gioco. C'è pure la cosa scema a chiudere.

Lo consiglio vivamente, lo ritengo l'episodio più riuscito tra i quattro Aveyond.

As a life-long fan of the Aveyond series, I can say with certainty that this is an incredible game. However, it's not an Aveyond game. Yes there are references here and there in conversation, but the only thing that makes this game by definition an Aveyond game is the presence of the holy land of Aveyond itself. You could change the name of that place and erase the 5 or 6 references you get in passing and you wouldn't even know it was part of the series. Like I said before I don't think this is a bad game, but it just doesn't have the feeling of being on a proper quest to save the world. In every Aveyond prior to this, there has been a real threat of an evildoer plotting some grand plan, and you are sent on a quest to stop this from happening, running into all sorts of plot twists, tricky puzzles and difficult enemies along the way. In this game, [spoiler] you start off on a quest to find your dog, and even when the game seems to pull out the dramatic plot of an evil demon, [/spoiler] the main characters brush it off as a joke, leaving the whole plot lacking to feel of a real, important goal.

Another aspect of the game that I believe sets it aside for the rest of the series is the amount of consistencies of the series that were broken:
[list]
[*]There is little to no mention of Thais or the Pendragons
[*]The menus work in a completely different way (i.e. no numbers on health/mana bars when using items, an individual equip menu for every character in their profile instead of one equip menu for everyone, the unappealing new layout of the home menu (especially when trying to use keys to quickly navigate the screen) etc.)
[*]New interactions with spells (i.e. a spell may hit a random number of times, hit a random enemy/random enemies, hit the hero party etc).
[*]Plently of memorable item, monster and character sprites were removed (which seems petty, but alongside everything else it kind of just sealed the deal)
[/list]
I feel like any one of these things could be implemented without alienating the game from the series, but all 3 along with others I might not have said are definitely a rather large shock.

As I have already eluded to, I also believe this game relies too much on it's comedic value to hold the player's interest in the plot (and the game as a whole). I had my fair share of good laughs during the Orbs of Magic series (usually during exchanges between Te'ijal and Galahad), and yes they made the games all the more enjoyable and added a sense of personality to the characters, but what keeps me going back to those games (as well as Aveyond 1 and 2) is the sense of completion I get every time I complete a quest, defeat a difficult enemy or ultimately finish the game. But because of all the satire and lack of suspense as to the final boss' plans, I found myself at the end of this game without even realising it. The feeling of approaching the climax of the story (i.e. the final showdown to stop your enemy's plan once and for all) just wasn't there. The fact that so many quests are left out of your journal for you to figure out on your own (i.e. [spoiler] the whole ordeal involving the two wizards and their towers [/spoiler]) didn't help either, as I went into the final fight fully expecting futher story development involving those side quests that I had assumed would come up later. (Please note that I am not saying the unwritten side quests were a negative addition. They are a great source of replay value and add that extra sense of completion to the game. However they should probably be pushed further to the side so as to not interfere with the apparent progression of the main storyline, or else they may actually withdraw from the sense of completion as it did with me).

Another note that I should make is that the number of highly problematic bugs in the game (at least at the time I played it) is rather alarming. Some characters don't show up during cutscenes, images may be doubled (i.e. [spoiler] a tile showing glowing eyes in a hollow tree shows a duplicate beneath itself on the misty mountain as the start of the game [/spoiler] ). And even carrying certain items interfered with menu interactions.

I have played all the Aveyond games and I have loved them all... except for this one. That's not to say it isn't an okay game, but it didn't live up to the expectations I have come to have for an Aveyond game. It was a bit disappointing.

Pros:
 - The characters are well done. Boyle makes for a fun and interesting "hero". The side characters are just as interesting and the dialog is well written..
 - The art is, as usual, beautiful. Each location has so many little details that make the map come alive.
 - The mechanics are great. Each character has their own set of unique skills. Changing one active party member for another can have a real impact in a fight.
 - The humor is on point.
 - Lots of little easter eggs / throwbacks to previous Aveyond games.

Cons:
 - The quests were all over the place, to the point it became confusing in parts. While a game can be boring if it is too linear, this game would have benefitted from more clear direction.
 - The story started out strong, but fell apart toward the middle. 
 - Backtracking. A lot of tedious back and forth, zig zagging all over. It got pretty boring.
 - The locations, while beautiful, felt small and cramped. The overall world map felt like each continent / island was stuck together on a too-small map at the end. Where previous games felt open and vast, this one felt small and squished.
 - The ending. No spoilers, but it was a letdown. I kept saying to myself "That's it?". Pretty disappointing.

Overall, the game started out strong but seemed to lose it's way around the middle. I enjoyed it for the most part, but I felt as though the game had potential to be better than it was. If you love the Aveyond games, by all means get the game. Maybe wait until it's on sale though.

Primary Issues:
Only two screen sizes, full screen and tiny. Full screen stretches the game for wide screen.

Audio slider for sound does not work.


Positives:
Story starts out fun and strong. Loses some focus in the middle but never becomes tedium.
Mechanics are an embaressment of riches. Every character has their own.
The meta dungeon was inventive. Cool idea well executed.
Being able to steal anything on the usuable item table was great.

Slow movement:
Late game there's no teleportation between cities, there is a system to reduce how much walking you need to do to get where you want to go but for this whole game you will be walking from point A to point B. 很久之前就接触 Aveyond 系列的游戏，玩第一部的时候觉得还不错，经过这么多年已经出到第四部了。

第三部到第四部之间隔的时间真得挺久的，不知道什么时候开始官网上的 Aveyond 4 就一直写着 Coming Soon，经过这么多年终于新鲜出炉了，作为老玩家表示这一代的 Aveyond 绝对是厚积薄发，没有让我失望！

在主线剧情方面上 Aveyond 4 延续了前作的风格，有经典 JRPG 的特点，并且[b]依然[/b]是主角拯救世界。不过故事展开的方式有了一些变化，主角不像是前作那样出身于普通人，而是征服世界未遂的 Boyle the Horrible。故事在散播正能量的同时也有很强的讽刺意味，打算征服世界的 Boyle 和拯救世界的英雄 Herclues 的实际身份完全反了过来。不得不再一次感叹编剧的想象力。

但是感觉 Aveyond 系列的气氛慢慢由严肃转为逗比，在 Aveyond 3 以后更是如此。在看 Aveyond 4 开场动画的时候笑出声，并不是因为它真的幽默，而是感觉一开始的 Boyle 作为反派，给人一种“坏到傻”的感觉。剧情中的角色也会不分场合地开各种玩笑，就连国王都是一副不正经的样子。这让我感觉是在看一出闹剧，虽然很欢乐，但是感觉总是不对。相比之下我还是喜欢 Aveyond 1 的那种严肃向的感觉。

人物刻画方面做得很不错，Boyle 和 Ingrid 这一对冤家简直太逗了，还有 Robin 这个年轻的骑士简直就是傻白甜。剧情中的 NPC 也是非常有趣的，而且不同地区的 NPC 的性格非常不同，这也是 Aveyond 系列的一大特色，希望能继续保持下去。

游戏细节部分制作得非常好，首先地图画质上和 3 代相比有了巨大的提升，并且也加了很多“特技”，人物行走图上还有一些细微动作，感觉到了良心。我非常喜欢 Windy Hills 那里的吊索桥的设计，主角走上去桥会微微晃动一下，感觉很逼真。人物经过不同区域的行走速度都会发生变化，爬梯子人会背过身去，还有脚步声的细节，都非常不错。

Aveyond 4 的可玩性非常高，并且我感觉它的解谜成分是所有 Aveyond 系列中最多的，皇宫地下洞窟的迷宫设计得很棒，精灵村图书馆的解谜也很有趣，相比于 Aveyond 1 里面吸血鬼村的那几个猜谜，简直好太多了。战斗系统也是改进了许多，我记得 3 代之前的回合制几乎没有任何的改动，到了 4 代战斗系统终于改了，加了一些新奇的玩法，我想说这不是早就应该这么做了么……支线的任务也蛮丰富的，奖励也不错，最后，好感度系统依然是那么简陋。另外这游戏像 Aveyond 3-4 一样，金钱资源非常稀少，十分考验大家的经济头脑。

说句题外话，Aveyond 4 里面的很多内容都和前作有关系，可能是向前作致敬，不过也可能是制作组在偷懒。但是无论如何，Aveyond 4 如果在玩前作的梗的话，那么刚接触此作品的玩家就会一脸懵逼。首先，依然是万年老梗 Te'ijal 和 Galahad，他们两位出现在 Aveyond [b]所有[/b]系列当中，虽然我承认我比较喜欢 T 姐和 G 叔（称呼好像有什么不对），但是，你们能不能换一些人来客串？[strike]我知道过了这么久了能活下来的只有他俩，别人都老死了[/strike]还有就是 Two-Card Flip Game 里面的卡牌，虽然我玩到最后也不知道这游戏到底该怎么玩，但是里面的卡牌多数借鉴了 Aveyond 3 的人物，例如 Mel, Edward, Gyendal 等。还有 Robin 商店任务里的某个顾客说她怀念 Shaenir 的天气，Shaenir 其实是 Aveyond 2 里面唯一的一个北方城市。总之看到这些梗老玩家表示很亲切，新玩家就算是懵逼也不太影响对剧情的理解吧（大概

好了下面说说 Aveyond 4 的问题。首先我玩通关之后表示剧情气氛是个硬伤，这部游戏从头到尾所有的角色几乎都在讲笑话，这真不是件好事情。然后就是主线里面有某些严重拖延剧情的现象，虽然有传送系统但是主角的移动速度真是太慢了，还是有很多时间花在了跑路上（雾灵妹子上下梯子不减速我也是才知道的）。这个游戏我卡过一次关，就是在解救 Hi'beru 返回 Tor 那里。说实话我真没找到第二个大陆的 Port 在哪，后来一顿瞎找终于在一个很[spoiler]哔[/spoiler]的地方找到了那个 Port 我想说制作组你们是不是故意把 Port 画成那样好让我们看不见的？

总之，Aveyond 4 是一款非常棒的游戏，无论新玩家还是老玩家，都值得去体验一下。

Best of the Aveyond titles thus far. The humor and references to RPGs in general are the best part. It's fun to play a retired villian finding his puppy (wolf minion).

If you're a fan of the previous Aveyond games, you'll enjoy this one. If you've never played them before, you'll still enjoy this one! Its a shorter RPG, or at least it feels like it, and the writing and humor are wonderful. The "fast travel" isn't really fast, which is kind of a problem, and so there's a lot of walking with no real way to make it go faster, A few of the puzzles and sidequests are a bit obtuse at times, but thankfully the creator's website has the answers to just about all of them, if you don't feel like buying the strategy guide. 

A few of the jokes will be funnier if you've played previous installments but this is largely unconnected to the previous three games in the series and easy to enjoy if you're new to the series. (Just remember, if you do go back to play the other games, that the first two are nearly ten years old now and the age shows.)
